# submodule　`def.submodule`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.submodule)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.submodule.md)

Kernels and images of module homomorphisms are submodules; a left ideal of $A$ is exactly a submodule of the left $A$-module $A$.

## Notes · **stale**
⭐ Three-level comparison: subgroup (group) ⊂ submodule (module) ⊂ subspace (module over a field). A submodule is required to be closed under the **ring action**, one condition more than "additive subgroup".

⭐ Examples: for $A = \mathbb{Z}$, submodules are the subgroups $n\mathbb{Z}$; for $A = K[x]$, submodules are the $K[x]$-subspaces.
